# Independent audit: the actual sum-of-own-depth counterexample



## Exact endpoint geometry and measures

For fixed \(S=x_2+\cdots+x_8\), the first-coordinate interval of \(D\) is
\[
 [0,11/18]\cap[7/18-S,1-S].
\]
Its length is exactly \(11/18-|S-7/18|\), including both endpoint regimes. It stays positive over the complete seven-dimensional cube. Reflection about the specified center swaps every coordinate-bound pair and sends the total sum to \(25/18\) minus itself, swapping its two bounds. The center is strictly interior.

The Fubini normalization by \(9^{-7}\) and the additional factor \(1/9\) in the absolute deviation are correct. The positive-orthant hinge integral is an eight-dimensional simplex volume; inclusion-exclusion over the seven bounded coordinates gives exactly the displayed expectation and volume. The rational diagonal scale has positive determinant and yields precisely \(|C|=2\Gamma V\), while retaining central symmetry. The common-coordinate and total-sum bounds used later follow from \(0<q<1\).

The small endpoint is a full cube of volume \(\epsilon^8\). Nonnegative coordinates and the exact sum bound \(123/125<1\) place the whole endpoint midpoint body in \(B\). The convex hull therefore has exactly the three prescribed positive integer fibers. It is full-dimensional and is exactly the hull of its mixed source. All masses are ordinary eight-volume, hence the actual intrinsic source measure is \(H_8\).

The own-depth values of the symmetric endpoints are exactly half their volumes. The simplex value follows from its centroid lower bound and canonical cap cover. Thus the proposed aggregate threshold is exactly \(\Gamma V+a/4\).

## Every middle candidate and the actual cap budgets

The two high-coordinate caps capture all of the small endpoint and strictly exclude the large endpoint, including its boundary. Each has middle volume \(V(1-b_h)^8\). For each of the seven low-coordinate caps, the maximum functional value on either endpoint is the same number \(\epsilon/2+\lambda/9\). The stated rational gap \(>1/720\) is correct, so both endpoints are strictly excluded and the middle cap mass is exactly \(V(1-b_l)^8\).

The thresholds sum to one, which makes these nine closed traces cover the entire middle simplex. This is a cover of every possible candidate point, not a calculation at one selected center.

Taylor's upper bound uses second derivative at most \(56\), hence remainder at most \(28h^2\). The bounds \(k,\ell<1/3\) give the coefficient \(28/9\). Both linear coefficients are exactly \(2/9\). The resulting difference from \(a/4\) is strictly greater than \((37/1500)a\), with all dimensional and \(V\)-normalizations correct.

## Endpoint candidates and the global conclusion

The four displayed endpoint half-caps cover their respective fibers. The finite coefficient-two tilts strictly exclude both other fibers in every case. Their actual masses are \(a/2\) and \(\Gamma V\), each below the common upper budget of the nine middle caps.

Thus the thirteen fixed ambient caps cover the entire actual source and each has the required budget. This proves the claimed strict upper bound on maximum mixed depth without assuming minimizing-cap attainment or using constrained capacities in place of volume.

The separate endpoint-centroid lower bound \(\Gamma V\) exceeds the original OC target exactly when \(\alpha<1-2\Gamma\), as verified. The example is therefore a counterexample only to the stronger sum-of-own-depth inequality. It has positive depth-root midpoint slack and does not conflict with the newly proved rigidity for equality in ordinary depth Brunn--Minkowski.
